newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro bourses gain, gold slips, dollar firm.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro bourses gain, gold slips, dollar firm.

text.p: Key European stock markets, spurred on by Wall Street's buoyant performance overnight, broke more records in morning business on Wednesday before easing back from their highs.
But gold, at 3-1/4 year lows below $353 an ounce, was down around $5 from overnight levels after investment funds took flight from the bullion market in New York.
News on Monday that the Dutch central bank had sold 300 tonnes of gold continues to hang over the market, prompting fears that other central banks could follow suit, analysts said.
"We may see a minor bounce but overall the market is firmly locked in a downside move...most people are looking to sell, while few are willing to buy," a bullion trader said.
Gold, depressed by competition from a firm dollar and booming share markets, has dropped about $15 this year.
On the currency market, the dollar strengthened to 1.5979 marks, its highest level against the German currency since July 1994, and a 46-month high of 117.47 yen.

"Dollar/mark is still quite well bid along with dollar/yen, although there are some sellers at these high levels. The market's just consolidating now and waiting for New York to come in," said a trader at a German bank.
Hoping that a dose of higher interest rates would not be needed just yet, London, Frankfurt, Paris and several other bourses moved up smartly into uncharted territory.

But unexpectedly strong British economic data, showing a marked drop in the jobless total, later jangled a few nerves and sent London, Europe's busiest stock market, into the minus column by the end of the morning.
"Everybody is now saying a rate rise is not going to happen but I don't think it's quite as clear cut as that," one London share trader said.

However, U.S. stocks in London made new gains, led by chip maker Intel after higher-than-expected earnings. This suggested that Wall Street could make more progress after the Dow Jones industrial average rose 53.11 to a record 6,762.29 on Tuesday.
"U.S. shares in London are mostly up," one dealer said. "The Dow should be higher to start with and after that, who knows?"

The London stock market, where the value of blue chips in the FTSE 100 index had added 111 points or about 18.8 billion pounds ($31.4 billion) in the week's two previous sessions, rose at the start but slipped back after the jobless figures.

Unemployment fell 45,100 in December to a six-year low of 1.88 million. "The unemployment fall was too high and the City (of London) is still split on interest rates," said a trader as nervousness returned after sharp recent gains.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke meets Eddie George, the Governor of the Bank of England, from 1500 GMT to discuss monetary policy.

British interest rates are expected to rise before an election, which must be held by mid-May, but had not generally been tipped to go up just yet. However, some analysts said a rate rise could not be ruled out after the jobs data.

In Frankfurt, Germany's blue-chip DAX index neared the elusive 3,000-point level after hitting a new all-time high in early bourse dealings -- although much of the gain had taken place in after-hours computerised trade on Tuesday.
Shares were boosted by a general market boom, benign U.S. consumer price data and the dollar's rally, which made stars of chemical shares and other dollar-sensitive stocks.
"A dollar at this level is going to mean windfall profits for a lot of companies and we will see that reflected in earnings statements at the year end," said one Frankfurt dealer.
Paris stocks also pushed to new highs, aided by the advance on Wall Street and higher bonds, before paring gains later.
Following Tuesday's all-time highs by a dozen bourses, Amsterdam, Athens, Brussels, Copenhagen, Lisbon, Stockholm and Zurich were also at or near new peaks on Wednesday morning.
In Asian trading, Hong Kong stocks also surged to record highs but Japanese markets, which have provided plenty of interest for those elsewhere recently, were on holiday.
CURRENCIES AT 1230 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 117.35 yen and 1.5975 marks, compared with 116.92 and 1.5957 late in Europe on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1230 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of key British stocks was down 0.6 point at 4,167.6, below an earlier record high of 4,191.5.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index was up 39.27 at 2,988.15.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 6.98 points higher at 2,409.12.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold slid to a morning fix of $352.45 an ounce, its lowest setting since October 4, 1993, from the previous London close of $357.55. Silver slipped five cents to $4.66.
